name: Learn: Labels, Selectors & Annotations
objective: CKAD core: label and annotate objects, and target them with equality + set-based selectors. Add/overwrite/remove labels, bulk-label via a selector, set-based matching, matchExpressions selectors, annotations, and a selector-mismatch diagnose-fix. Graded exactly.
description: Seven strict practicals on labels/selectors/annotations against pre-seeded pods. Each Check shows which requirements you met and why any failed.

questions.title: Add a label
questions.teach:
`kubectl label <kind>/<name> key=value` attaches a label (key/value metadata used for selecting and grouping objects).

**Gotcha:** labelling an existing key without `--overwrite` fails — add fails loudly rather than clobbering.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add the label `env=prod` to pod `frontend`.

Target: pod `frontend` has label `env=prod`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label pod frontend env=prod
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend --show-labels

questions.title: Overwrite and remove a label
questions.teach:
Change an existing label with `kubectl label --overwrite key=newvalue`; remove one with `kubectl label <obj> key-` (trailing dash).

**Gotcha:** without `--overwrite`, relabelling an existing key errors; `key-` (not `key=`) is how you delete a label.
questions.prompt:
Pod `legacy` in `labels-learn` has labels `env=dev` and `deprecated=true`. **Overwrite** `env` to `prod`, and **remove** the `deprecated` label.

Target: pod `legacy` has `env=prod` and no `deprecated` label.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n labels-learn label --overwrite pod legacy env=prod` and `kubectl -n labels-learn label pod legacy deprecated-`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label --overwrite pod legacy env=prod
kubectl -n labels-learn label pod legacy deprecated-
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod legacy --show-labels

questions.title: Bulk-label via a selector
questions.teach:
Label many objects at once by targeting them with `-l <selector>`: `kubectl label pods -l app=shop tier=web` labels every pod matching `app=shop`.

**Gotcha:** `-l` on `kubectl label` selects *which* objects to label — it doesn't set that label.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add the label `tier=web` to **all** pods that match `app=shop` (there are two), in one command.

Target: every `app=shop` pod has `tier=web`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label pods -l app=shop tier=web
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods -l app=shop --show-labels

verification.description: all app=shop pods now have tier=web

questions.title: Set-based selector targeting
questions.teach:
Set-based selectors match against a set of values: `-l 'release in (beta,rc)'`, `notin (...)`, or `key`/`!key` (exists / not-exists). Use them to target a subset.

**Gotcha:** quote the selector in the shell; equality (`=`,`!=`) and set-based (`in`,`notin`) can be combined with commas.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add `canary=yes` to every pod whose `release` is **in (beta, rc)** — using a set-based selector. The `release=stable` pod must NOT get it.

Target: `rel-beta` and `rel-rc` have `canary=yes`; `rel-stable` does not.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn label pods -l 'release in (beta,rc)' canary=yes
kubectl -n labels-learn get pods -L release -L canary

questions.title: A selector with matchExpressions
questions.teach:
A controller/Service selector can use `matchExpressions` for set-based rules: `{key: app, operator: In, values: [exp]}` (operators `In`/`NotIn`/`Exists`/`DoesNotExist`), optionally alongside `matchLabels`.

**Gotcha:** the pod template's labels must satisfy the selector, or the Deployment is rejected.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, create a Deployment `exp` (image `nginx:1.25`, 1 replica, pod label `app=exp`) whose **selector uses matchExpressions**: key `app`, operator `In`, values `[exp]`.

Target: Deployment `exp` selector has a matchExpressions rule `app In [exp]`, and its pods are labelled `app=exp`.
questions.hint: `spec.selector.matchExpressions: [{key: app, operator: In, values: [exp]}]`; pod template `labels: {app: exp}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: exp, namespace: labels-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchExpressions: [ { key: app, operator: In, values: [ exp ] } ]
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: exp } }
    spec:
      containers: [ { name: web, image: nginx:1.25 } ]
YAML

verification.description: Deployment exp selector matchExpressions app In [exp]

questions.title: Annotate an object
questions.teach:
`kubectl annotate <obj> key=value` attaches non-identifying metadata. Unlike labels, **annotations can't be used in selectors** — they're for tools, descriptions, and controller hints.

**Gotcha:** labels are selectable + size-limited; annotations are not selectable but hold larger/arbitrary data.
questions.prompt:
In `labels-learn`, add the annotation `owner=team-a` to pod `frontend`.

Target: pod `frontend` has annotation `owner=team-a`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn annotate pod frontend owner=team-a
kubectl -n labels-learn get pod frontend -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.owner}'

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a selector that matches nothing
questions.teach:
A Service with **no endpoints** despite healthy pods means its selector doesn't match any pod labels. Compare `kubectl get svc <s> -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` to `kubectl get pods --show-labels` and loosen/fix the selector.

**Gotcha:** removing a selector key via patch needs `key: null` (a plain merge keeps it).
questions.prompt:
Service `shop-svc` in `labels-learn` selects `app=shop,tier=cache` — but no pod has `tier=cache`, so it has zero endpoints. Fix the selector so it fronts the `app=shop` pods. Don't delete it.

Target: `shop-svc` has at least one endpoint.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n labels-learn get svc shop-svc -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` shows `tier: cache`. Remove it: `kubectl -n labels-learn patch svc shop-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","tier":null}}}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n labels-learn patch svc shop-svc -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","tier":null}}}'
kubectl -n labels-learn get endpoints shop-svc -o wide
